name: IN-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by about 15 points
Houchin holds a roughly 20-to-1 fundraising advantage
Prediction markets give Democrats only about a 3 percent chance
No public polls or expert ratings; race draws little attention
model.rationale: A strongly Republican district, an incumbent who has raised more than $2.1 million against a challenger with about $105,000, and prediction markets pricing Democrats near 3 percent all point the same direction, so the fundamentals-based estimate of a 16-point Houchin win stands without adjustment.
model.watch: A large national Democratic wave or a late outside-spending surge could narrow the margin, though no such signs are currently present.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Erin Houchin, the Republican incumbent, defends a southern Indiana seat that leans Republican by about 15 points. She has raised more than $2.1 million and holds $1.27 million on hand, while Democratic challenger Brad Meyer has raised roughly $105,000 with under $20,000 available. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot with minimal resources. No public polling covers the general election and no expert raters list the race, but prediction markets give Democrats only about a 3 percent chance of winning.

District partisanship, incumbency, and the lopsided money race all point toward a comfortable Republican win. National conditions could shift the margin at the edges, but nothing in the available evidence suggests the seat is seriously contested. The forecast expects Houchin to prevail by roughly 16 points.
